No, don't do that. kubectl delete -f install/cluster-operator is the Strimzi uninstall command, and that directory contains the CRDs. Deleting a CRD deletes every custom resource of that type. That means the Kafka, KafkaNodePool, KafkaTopic and KafkaUser resources of core and dr, and with them the Kubernetes resources they manage can go too. It would not be a reinstall without downtime; you would be taking down both production clusters.

What went wrong is one skipped step. The release's RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding files don't name your operator namespace, and the upgrade procedure has you set it before applying. You replaced the bindings unchanged, so they now point at a service account that isn't yours. That is why the operator logs forbidden. Fix the files and run the upgrade again:
1. sed -i 's/namespace: .*/namespace: strimzi-system/' install/cluster-operator/*RoleBinding*.yaml
2. Keep STRIMZI_NAMESPACE=kafka,kafka-dr in 060-Deployment-strimzi-cluster-operator.yaml.
3. kubectl replace -f install/cluster-operator -n strimzi-system
4. Create the 020, 023 and 031 RoleBindings in kafka and kafka-dr with kubectl create -f ... -n <namespace>.

There is no hurry. The upgrade doesn't affect cluster availability, and while the operator can't reconcile, the brokers keep running unreconciled. Afterwards, check that the operator log has no forbidden errors, that kubectl get kafka -A shows both clusters Ready, and wait for the rolling updates to finish.

Do not merge the PR. The growth comes from clickstream-enriched: its KafkaTopic, created nine days ago, sets retention.ms: -1, so no time limit applies and it keeps everything (about 340 GB on broker 0, all written in nine days).

The PR would not even touch that topic. log.retention.hours is a broker default and applies only to topics without their own setting; clickstream-enriched has retention.ms: -1, which overrides it. What the PR would do is delete, at the next retention check, every closed segment older than 48 hours of every topic on the default. invoices is one of them: billing-weekly-export has not read the last four days (about 400,000 records per partition), so those invoices would be gone and the group's offsets would point at deleted data, to be reset by auto.offset.reset.

Fix it where it is defined:
1. Ask the owners for the retention they need and set it in the KafkaTopic in Git, for example spec.config.retention.ms: 259200000 (three days). Do not use kafka-configs.sh: the Topic Operator reverts changes made outside the KafkaTopic.
2. The closed segments older than three days are removed at the next retention check (log.retention.check.interval.ms, five minutes by default).
3. If you need headroom before that, raise size in the brokers KafkaNodePool (for example 1500Gi); gp3-kafka allows expansion, and the Cluster Operator restarts the pods once the volumes are resized.
4. Watch the volumes fall back to about 55% and keep log.retention.hours at 168.

Don't remove the probes; add a startup probe.

What is happening: kafka-2 stopped without a clean shutdown, so it has to run log recovery over 1.6 TB before it serves requests. The liveness probe allows 60 s plus three failures and restarts it before the recovery has finished; the broker never gets to a clean shutdown, so the next start must recover again, and so it loops.

The fix is a startupProbe with the same command and failureThreshold x periodSeconds above your worst recovery time, for example:
  startupProbe: (same exec)
    periodSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 180   # 30 minutes
While a startup probe is configured, Kubernetes runs no liveness or readiness probe until it succeeds; afterwards the liveness probe still catches a hung broker. The long initialDelaySeconds on liveness can then go.

Keep the readiness probe in particular. Your StatefulSet's RollingUpdate waits for each updated pod to be Running and Ready before it restarts the next one. A container without a readiness probe counts as ready as soon as it runs, so the next chart upgrade would restart brokers back to back while earlier ones are still recovering, and partitions with two replicas on those brokers would refuse acks=all writes or go offline.

Optionally raise num.recovery.threads.per.data.dir (2 by default) to shorten recovery, at the cost of more disk I/O. After merging, watch kafka-2 log the end of recovery and rejoin the ISR before you touch any other broker.
